featured.title: Why healthy teeth help your pet live longer
featured.description: Worried about your pet's breath? Proper oral care not only reduces odor but also prevents heart, liver and kidney disease in dogs and cats.
featured.content:
Oral care is about much more than breath. Long-term tartar buildup lets bacteria enter the bloodstream and attack your pet's heart, liver and kidneys.

Brush your pet's teeth 2–3 times a week with dedicated toothpaste, and schedule an oral check every 6 months.

At PetShop, our deep oral hygiene service removes light tartar and advises on the right care for each breed.

lifestyle.title: Balancing life and time for your pet
lifestyle.description: Small habits that help even busy owners care for their pet well every day without feeling overwhelmed.
lifestyle.content:
A busy life does not mean giving your pet less attention. Just 15 minutes a day of brushing, walking or play is enough for your pet to feel loved.

Set a fixed care schedule — bath, trimming, hygiene — so you never forget and always keep your pet healthy and clean.

sidebar.title: Keeping your pet safe on a long trip
sidebar.content:
Before a long trip, bring water, familiar food and a well-fitting carrier. Stop every 2–3 hours so your pet can move and drink.

Do not forget vaccination records and an ID tag with your contact phone number.

sidebar.title: 5 common mistakes when bathing your dog at home
sidebar.content:
Bathing too often, using human shampoo, getting water in the ears, not brushing out tangles and not drying thoroughly are common mistakes.

Bathe every 2–4 weeks with dedicated shampoo and always dry the ears well.

sidebar.title: 5 seemingly harmless foods that harm cats
sidebar.content:
Onion, garlic, grapes, chocolate and cow milk can all harm cats even though they look harmless.

If you suspect your cat ate any of these, contact a vet immediately instead of treating at home.

sidebar.title: How PetShop contacts you — and how we never will
sidebar.content:
We only call or message via Zalo at 0971 616 634 to confirm appointments.

PetShop never asks for your password, OTP code or a bank transfer deposit via message.

sidebar.title: Understanding the real cost of owning a pet
sidebar.content:
Pet costs fall into three main groups: food, preventive healthcare and grooming.

A monthly budget keeps you in control and avoids surprises when your pet gets sick.

sidebar.title: Letting go of the pressure to buy expensive pet items
sidebar.content:
Pets do not need many expensive accessories — what they need most is your time and attention.

Choose the essentials with good quality instead of chasing trends.

sidebar.title: When should you take your cat to the spa?
sidebar.content: Cats groom themselves, so they rarely need bathing. Take your cat to the spa when their coat is matted, smelly, or a vet recommends medicated shampoo.
